edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Σπουδάζετε οὖν βεβαιωθῆναι ἐν τοῖς δόγμασιν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων, ἵνα πάντα, ὅσα ποιεῖτε, κατευοδωθῆτε σαρκὶ καὶ πνεύματι, πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ, ἐν υἱῷ καὶ πατρὶ καὶ ἐν πνεύματι, ἐν ἀρχῇ καὶ ἐν τέλει, μετὰ τοῦ ἀξιοπρεπεστάτου ἐπισκόπου ὑμῶν καὶ ἀξιοπλόκου πνευματικοῦ στεφάνου τοῦ πρεσβυτερίου ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν κατὰ θεὸν διακόνων. [2] ὑποτάγητε τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ ἀλλήλοις, ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρὶ καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῷ πατρὶ ἵνα ἕνωσις ᾖ σαρκική τε καὶ πνευματική.
pass_a_gloss: Be eager, then, to be made firm in the decrees of the Lord and of the apostles, so that in everything you do you may prosper, in flesh and spirit, in faith and love, in the Son and the Father and in the Spirit, in the beginning and in the end, together with your most worthy bishop, and the worthily woven spiritual crown of your presbytery, and the deacons who are godly. Be subject to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ was to the Father, and the apostles to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a union both of flesh and of spirit.
pass_b_english: Strive, then, to be established in the teachings of the Lord and of the apostles, so that you may prosper in all you do: in flesh and in spirit, in faith and in love, in the Son and the Father and the Spirit, at the beginning and at the end. May you prosper together with your bishop, most worthy of honor, with your presbytery, that finely woven spiritual crown, and with your godly deacons.
Submit to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ submitted to the Father, and as the apostles submitted to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a union of flesh and of spirit alike.

choices.why: δόγμα here is authoritative decree or teaching, not later technical 'dogma'.
Rare compound for a wreath well plaited; the presbyters ring the bishop like a crown.
The first pair is the whole person, lowercase; the second stands in the Son-Father-Spirit triad and is capitalized.

choices.english: so that there may be a union of flesh and of spirit alike
choices.why: Keeps his pairing of bodily and spiritual unity.

anf_compare.notes: ANF adds 'according to the flesh' after 'as Jesus Christ to the Father' and 'and to the Spirit' after 'to Christ and to the Father'. Neither phrase stands in the Lake Greek as supplied (apparatus stripped); they may be bracketed or variant readings. We translate only the supplied text.

notes: 'Be subject ... to one another' may echo Ephesians 5:21; not cited inline.
Check Lake's apparatus for κατὰ σάρκα and καὶ τῷ πνεύματι in 13.2 before locking.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] matches Magnesians 13 as locked. 'Σπουδάζετε οὖν βεβαιωθῆναι ἐν τοῖς δόγμασιν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων' = A 'Be eager, then, to be made firm in the decrees of the Lord and of the apostles' and B 'Strive, then, to be established in the teachings of the Lord and of the apostles' (passive kept; δόγμα as decree/teaching). 'ἵνα πάντα, ὅσα ποιεῖτε, κατευοδωθῆτε σαρκὶ καὶ πνεύματι, πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ, ἐν υἱῷ καὶ πατρὶ καὶ ἐν πνεύματι, ἐν ἀρχῇ καὶ ἐν τέλει, μετὰ τοῦ ἀξιοπρεπεστάτου ἐπισκόπου ὑμῶν καὶ ἀξιοπλόκου πνευματικοῦ στεφάνου τοῦ πρεσβυτερίου ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν κατὰ θεὸν διακόνων' = A 'so that in everything you do you may prosper, in flesh and spirit, in faith and love, in the Son and the Father and in the Spirit, in the beginning and in the end, together with your most worthy bishop, and the worthily woven spiritual crown of your presbytery, and the deacons who are godly'. B keeps the same spheres and companions; 'May you prosper together with your bishop, most worthy of honor, with your presbytery, that finely woven spiritual crown, and with your godly deacons' only resumes κατευοδωθῆτε for the μετὰ phrase, without a new agent or claim. Lowercase flesh/spirit vs capitalized triad Spirit is kept. [2] 'ὑποτάγητε τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ ἀλλήλοις, ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρὶ καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῷ πατρὶ ἵνα ἕνωσις ᾖ σαρκική τε καὶ πνευματική' = A 'Be subject to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ was to the Father, and the apostles to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a union both of flesh and of spirit' and B 'Submit to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ submitted to the Father, and as the apostles submitted to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a union of flesh and of spirit alike'. No negation is flipped. No inline citation is wrong. Title 'Firm in the Lord's Teachings' names the thought, not only the locus.

Source identity confirmed: Ignatius, Magnesians 13, Lake 1912 Loeb. Completeness: all clauses from Locked Greek [1] covered in Pass A and B. Negation: none present. Doctrine: Trinitarian structure (Son, Father, Spirit) and ecclesial hierarchy maintained. Scripture: no inline citations in source; notes correctly state possible Ephesians 5:21 echo is not cited.
